method: All searching used gh read-only against the seven upstream repos (search API for PRs, issues and commits; REST for PR metadata, PR file lists and patches, commit parents and file contents at a ref; GraphQL only to read closedByPullRequestsReferences for a11y issues). Pass 1: the 28 terms (a11y, accessibility, accessible, "screen reader", VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS, aria-label, aria, "alt text", alt, label, keyboard, "keyboard navigation", focus, "focus trap", "focus ring", "focus visible", tabindex, "tab order", role, contrast, WCAG, axe, "accessible name", announce, "live region", "reduced motion") against merged PRs in every repo (title and body), plus closed issues with a linked PR for a11y, accessibility, "screen reader" and keyboard; the closing PRs of promising issues were read through GraphQL. Pass 2: because the react-spectrum PR template and the supabase bot summaries mention accessibility, body search was saturated there, so 18 react-spectrum and 17 supabase terms were re-run with in:title; commit search was run for shadcn-ui/ui, radix-ui/primitives, excalidraw and next.js (shadcn often lands fixes as direct commits), and the REST commit list for packages/react-aria-components/src (544 commits) was grepped for a11y words. Pass 3: a few extra terms (sr-only, aria-hidden, aria-describedby, DialogTitle, focus-visible, "screen readers"). Every candidate's diff was read. A fix was confirmed only if it was merged, changed UI code in the in-scope paths, and removed a barrier for screen reader, keyboard or low-vision users. For each confirmed fix, merged_at, merge_commit_sha and the merge commit's parent were read from the REST API (all confirmed PRs were squash or rebase merges with one parent, so parentSha is the pre-fix state of the base branch); the pre-fix file was downloaded at parentSha with the contents API, the barrier lines were located in it, and the code excerpts in `files` are copied verbatim from those downloads by script. Line numbers are at parentSha. expectedRules are judgments from reading the pre-fix code, not lint runs; jsx-a11y names follow oxlint's jsx-a11y plugin (as enabled in Ultracite's oxlint react preset) and Biome names are lint/a11y/*.

lintDrivenCleanups.note: Added 13 jsx-a11y rules to Studio's ESLint config as ratcheted warnings, after an axe-core audit found 1,733 failing elements across 126 Studio surfaces in 12 root-cause families. Initial baselines were mostly control-has-associated-label (274, with controlComponents Button and Switch) and label-has-associated-control (37). Config only, no .tsx changes.

'fix: ESLint errors relating to accessibility (alt attribute and tableEditor components)': clears ratchet findings in 5 .tsx files. The fixes are real (alt text, names) but were found and described as lint errors.
'fix: ESLint errors relating to accessibility in table editor, API Key and Access Token': aria-label and Tooltip on icon-only buttons, 6 .tsx files, driven by the ratchet.
'fix: ESLint errors relating to accessibility in account preferences': toggle labelling and aria-label, 4 .tsx files.
'fix: ESLint errors relating to accessibility in database section': aria-label and switch-to-label association, 7 .tsx files.
'fix: ESLint errors relating to accessibility in integration section': aria-label additions, 8 .tsx files.
'fix: ESLint errors relating to accessibility in project settings': aria-label and Tooltip for icon-only buttons, 5 .tsx files.

Baked an explicit tabIndex={0} into interactive primitives (Checkbox, bare triggers) for Safari's Tab behaviour and added a custom lint rule, supabase/require-explicit-tabindex, to keep raw <button> call sites from regressing. Follows the confirmed Switch fix #45083.

Promoted supabase/require-explicit-tabindex to error and added explicit tabIndex across www, docs and design-system (87 .tsx files). A repo-specific rule for a browser default that jsx-a11y and Biome do not model.

notes: trpc/trpc has no confirmed fixes: its packages/*/src .tsx files are hooks and providers (createTRPCReact, withTRPC, context) with no UI, and the two accessibility PRs found (#7302 link text, #6440 link contrast) are in the www docs site.

Body search was saturated where templates mention accessibility: in adobe/react-spectrum 'accessibility' matched 3,484 merged PRs and 'aria' 3,890 (the PR template links Aria Practices); title-only search cut those to 33 and 232. Supabase's CodeRabbit summaries add 'accessibility' to many bodies (435 body hits vs 23 in titles). Other noisy terms: alt (Alt-key and alt-drag features in excalidraw, 503 hits), label (GitHub labels and form labels everywhere), role (database roles in supabase, 1,120 hits), focus (binding focus points in excalidraw), announce (release announcements), axe (font axes in next.js).

shadcn-ui/ui: community accessibility PRs are often closed unmerged (#6798, #10078, #524, #1222 in `rejected`), and the maintainer lands fixes as direct commits. One direct commit is confirmed (shadcn-ui/ui@961e0b62d770, id uses @sha); it is on main (compare API: main ahead, behind_by 0) but has no PR, and only its calendar change has a recorded reason (contrast); the CardTitle h3 -> div change says only 'to improve accessibility'. Two shadcn fixes are outside today's corpus include paths: #12061 is in packages/shadcn/src/tailwind.css (the stylesheet the registry styles import) and #224/#2163/#2190/961e0b6 are in the older apps/www/components/ui and apps/www/registry paths.

Scope versus corpus: supabase fixes in packages/ui and packages/ui-patterns (#50083, #48527, #49345, #45083) are outside the corpus include list in repos-accessibility.json (apps/studio/components and pages only); react-spectrum #9888 is in @adobe/react-spectrum (v3), marked in `package`. The later lint script should fetch these files directly.

Chains worth telling: next.js #62723 turned a <span onClick> into a <button> but gave it tabIndex={10} and no name; #80289 removed the positive tabIndex and #80290 added the name, fifteen months later. next.js #76558 replaced unassociated <h2> captions with <label htmlFor>, including one on a <button>, which #77072 changed to aria-describedby. supabase #45083 (tabIndex on Switch for Safari) led to #47984 and #48170, a custom lint rule requiring explicit tabIndex on buttons.

Cheap attributes that satisfy a rule without fixing the barrier: supabase #48527's <label id={props.id} htmlFor={props.value}> passes label-has-associated-control because any htmlFor counts, though it pointed at an option value, not an element id. excalidraw #3871 and shadcn #2163 had aria-labels present but wrong (a hex code; 'Toggle italic' on a Bold button), which every name rule accepts. react-spectrum #5867's <div onClick> carried an eslint-disable-next-line on exactly the element whose click handler caused the focus bug; the suppressed rules were about key handlers, not focus. Conversely, supabase #49345's unnamed icon button would trip Biome's noSvgWithoutTitle on the inline <svg>, and a <title> there would have named the button.

Statically visible barriers were the minority (5 of 40 yes, 8 partly, 27 no). The 'yes' cases are all the same two patterns: a static element with onClick (excalidraw #3310 and #556, next.js #62723 and #92608) and a literal positive tabIndex (next.js #80289). Library code (radix, react-aria, shadcn primitives) almost never shows the barrier in JSX: props are spread, ids come from context, and names are dropped in hook arguments.

Valid fixes seen but not recorded in detail (to keep 30-40 entries spread across repos): next.js #76558/#77072 (preference selects without labels), #76525, #75736, #76490 (dev overlay contrast), #74563 (aria-live for feedback thanks), #70612 and #71420 (static indicator name and role), #75790 (outline: none on pagination buttons), #31147 (route announcer prefers document.title), #7693 (focus after Link navigation), #20428 (route announcer added); excalidraw #2341 (dialog focus trap ref), #644 (focus outline on radio labels), #12188 (zen mode stripped the focus-visible ring); radix #1469 (toast tab order), #3922 (aria-controls pointing at unmounted content), #4031 (broken ARIA references in dialogs); react-aria #9746 (TreeSection rendered as <section> with a row-group role), #8932; supabase #49637 and #50080 (FormItemLayout label for and description ids), #48303 (skip link invisible on focus), #50834, #50828, #47828, #40691, #42668 (contrast), #47214, #47531, #47639, #47674, #45981, #45790 (icon-button names from the axe audit), #43058 (heading anchors not focusable), #45064 (select fields skipped by Tab in Safari).

API use: 287 searches in all (224 in pass 1, 53 in pass 2, 10 in pass 3), paced at about one every 2.5 to 4 seconds. One search in pass 1 (adobe/react-spectrum 'accessibility') got a 403 secondary rate limit at 21:46 UTC on 2026-10-15, probably from another agent sharing the token; the script waited 30 seconds and retried successfully. The REST core quota was not exhausted. search/issues caps results at 100 per query, so for terms with more hits only the 100 best matches were read.
